adr: 0298 — A /ToUnicode CMap that builds on another, and the whole shortfall behind the text gate
review_scope: Current ToUnicode base resolution, reader-vs-writer meaning of UseCMap, and the issue5010 witness.
original_claim: Follow a ToUnicode base named by the stream dictionary or by the in-stream usecmap operator; an unknown base yields no answer rather than a hard failure.
current_evidence: `read_to_unicode` resolves dictionary stream/name references and also has the tolerant embedded-operator fallback. The inspected issue5010 fixture omits dictionary /UseCMap even though §9.7.5.4(a) requires the dictionary and operator to agree; ADR correctly treats it as invalid producer input and a robustness witness. Effective EC3 Table 125a expressly permits /UseCMap name or stream.
decision: Retain the distinction between the valid dictionary route and tolerant handling of the invalid corpus witness. The drafted exact-xref public test targets the valid stream route, which existing focused coverage did not demonstrate.
residuals: Run drafts/tounicode_usecmap_stream_inheritance.rs. No known defect in this route was found by static tracing; missing valid public coverage is the current finding.

adr: 0971 — The second parser over the same carried files
review_scope: Bounded ToUnicode mapping tables and reports for discarded mappings.
original_claim: Finite mapping limits are explicit, report a discarded mapping rather than a full-but-truncated result, and admit the carried Adobe CMap population.
current_evidence: `MAX_SINGLES`, `MAX_RANGES`, `MAX_OPERANDS`, `cut_by`, and the ledger's population census are distinct from the two representation defects here. The drafts use only tiny maps; no bound is reached.
decision: No change suggested to the bound policy from this shard. Do not infer a requirement to process unbounded tables. The source-code-length and sequential string issues occur before any limit and can lose mappings in small valid inputs.
residuals: Full carried-file census and exact-bound behavior were not rerun; this review relies on current code and ledger evidence.

adr: 0426 — The erratum, a row recorded and never applied
review_scope: Whether EC3 Issue #462 is applied to §9.10.3 commentary and behavior.
original_claim: Correct stale quotations of the former single-entry stream-dictionary text and preserve the still-valid UseCMap behavior under Table 125a.
current_evidence: The current test commentary notes #462. Table 125a adds Type, CMapName, CIDSystemInfo, WMode, and UseCMap; code reads UseCMap, while the other fields are descriptive metadata for this extraction consumer. The source-code-length and destination mapping wording is unchanged.
decision: Retain the correction. Keep the new dictionary metadata distinct from mapping behavior; the error here is not an unimplemented reader requirement to validate those optional metadata entries.
residuals: This shard sampled §9.10.3 and did not audit the behavior of all CMap stream metadata consumers elsewhere.

adr: 0252 — The errata were in the file and the conversion dropped them
review_scope: EC3 source fidelity and corrected effective requirements.
original_claim: Use the combined ISO+EC3 source as effective text, not stale converted passages.
current_evidence: The processed EC3 document contains the replacement Table 125a and the existing §9.10.3 source-code and bfrange prose. The applied errata index records #462 for §9.10.3.
decision: No new erratum defect. The two candidate mapping gaps are present in the effective primary prose and do not depend on stale converted text.
residuals: Only #462 and the local source passages were checked for this bounded clause.
